channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Indian Rupee remains firm on early signs of FIIs return
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) reflects strength against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA pause keeps downside risks alive – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad reports that AUD/USD has retraced part of its US-Iran peace agreement rally after the Reserve Bank of Australia left rates unchanged at 4.35%.

item.title: US President Trump: We want to get Iran’s enriched uranium
item.description: United States (US) President Donald Trump said during the European trading session on Tuesday that psychologically, we want to get Iran’s enriched uranium.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA pause weighs on currency after strong gains – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman reports the Australian Dollar has weakened modestly after failing to reclaim the 0.7100 level and as the RBA unanimously left rates on hold at 4.35% following three hikes this year.

item.title: United States Dollar: Upside risks persist near range highs – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad notes the Dollar Index is trading defensively just below the top of its long-held 96.00–100.00 range, even as US assets benefit from optimism after the US-Iran peace agreement.

item.title: Euro edges up above 1.1600 after positive ZEW Economic Sentiment data
item.description: The Euro (EUR) holds a moderately positive tone against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, with the EUR/USD pair returning to levels above 1.1600, following upbeat economic sentiment data in Germany and the Eurozone.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Gradual BoJ tightening keeps currency under pressure – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes the Japanese Yen is little changed after the BoJ’s widely anticipated 0.25% rate hike to 1.00%, with USD/JPY still trading just above 160.00. The BoJ also decided to pause its QE taper from FY2027, while continuing gradual JGB purchase reductions until then.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Tuesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $70.51 per troy ounce, up 0.70% from the $70.02 it cost on Monday.

item.title: USD/CNH: Grind lower toward key support – UOB
item.description: Quek Ser Leang at UOB notes that USD/CNH’s earlier sharp decline has stalled into consolidation around 6.76, with intraday trading expected between 6.7540 and 6.7640.

item.title: Germany ZEW Survey - Economic Sentiment turns positive 10.5 in June: What it means for EUR/USD?
item.description: German ZEW Survey - Economic Sentiment turns positive to 10.5 in June after remaining negative in May. The data was expected to come in better at -6.0 from the previous reading of -10.2.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Clinging to 0.5800 support as risk appetite ebbs
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) posts marginal losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, trading at 0.5820 after bouncing up from session lows at 0.5795.

item.title: British Pound: Upside risks but momentum flattening – UOB
item.description: According to UOB’s Quek Ser Leang, GBP/USD stalled just below key resistance at 1.3465 and closed near 1.3410, with intraday momentum indicators turning flat.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Uptrend extends towards 1.4150 – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kenneth Broux highlights that USD/CAD has broken above a key descending trendline and the upper boundary of a multi‑month base, signalling renewed upside momentum.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed focus offsets oil slide – ING
item.description: ING strategists Francesco Pesole, Chris Turner and Frantisek Taborsky note the Dollar is rallying again, supported by strong US data and Federal Reserve expectations despite sharply lower Oil prices.

item.title: Euro: Upside bias capped by resistance – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang highlights that EUR/USD failed to sustain gains above 1.1620 and closed at 1.1590, with momentum slowing.

item.title: Gold: Recovery needs softer Oil and peak Fed repricing – OCBC
item.description: Christopher Wong at OCBC notes Gold has rebounded about 5% as US‑Iran de‑escalation eased Oil-led inflation and rates shocks. He cautions that upside momentum may slow into the FOMC, with further gains dependent on softer Oil, lower yields and evidence Fed hawkish repricing has peaked.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ path points to medium‑term gains – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Jin Kenzaki and team say the Bank of Japan’s hike to 1.0% marks only the bottom of the neutral range, but new language on upside inflation risks supports further normalisation.

item.title: Euro: Unstable floor with downside risks – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole highlights that EUR/USD has returned to Friday’s levels, with markets prioritizing central bank dynamics over Oil. A wider EUR:USD swap differential contrasts with weaker Eurozone growth and a less dovish Fed, limiting bullish Euro positioning.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah to extend recovery if BI stays firm – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Christopher Wong says recent surprise hikes and FX measures from Bank Indonesia have restored some confidence in the Rupiah.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Treading water around 1.3400 with central banks in focus
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) is trading practically flat against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Hawkish RBA fails to impress markets – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes that the Reserve Bank of Australia delivered a hawkish hold, stressing that inflation remains too high and further rate hikes are possible.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ hike fails to lift currency – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner says the Bank of Japan’s 25 bp hike to 1.00% is no game-changer for the Japanese Yen, as policy remains accommodative and real rates stay comfortably negative.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah rises as US Dollar trims recent gains despite risk-off mood
item.description: USD/IDR extends its losses for the second successive day, trading around 17,720 during the European hours on Tuesday. The pair loses ground as the US Dollar (USD) pares its daily gains despite prevailing market caution.

item.title: What is dragging the British Pound toward 1.3100 as political noise and stagflationary pressures mount?
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) is facing compounding pressures ahead of the Bank of England (BoE) interest-rate decision on Thursday. Financial markets have pushed back expectations for rate hikes to later in the year, leaving the currency highly sensitive to incoming economic data and geopolitics.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Needs breakout above 160.70 for fresh leg of rally
item.description: The USD/JPY pair ticks down to near 160.25 during the European trading session on Tuesday. The pair trades marginally lower as the Japanese Yen (JPY) outperforms its peers, following the Bank of Japan’s (BoJ) monetary policy announcement.

item.title: Australian Dollar edges up above 0.7050 amid hawkish comments by RBA's Bullock
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) remains on its back foot against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, although the pair has bounced up above 0.7050 after hitting session lows near 0.7040 following a monetary tightening pause by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA).

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Pulls back toward 185.50 near nine-day EMA
item.description: EUR/JPY depreciates after two days of gains, trading around 185.60 during the early European hours on Tuesday. The currency cross holds a mild bullish bias as it trades above the nine-day and 50-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs).

item.title: Forex Today: BoJ hikes, RBA holds, markets await details of US-Iran deal
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Tuesday, June 16:

item.title: Uchida Speech: BoJ Deputy Governor discusses policy outlook after the expected interest rate hike
item.description: Bank of Japan (BoJ) Deputy Governor Shinichi Uchida is addressing the press conference, explaining the reason behind raising the key interest rate by 25 basis points (bps) to 1.0% as expected.

item.title: Euro: EU-China trade and accession politics in focus – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Global Daily notes that the EU has formally launched accession talks with Ukraine and Moldova while simultaneously hardening its stance toward China.
